text: The rule of modus ponens is the only rule needed for a Hilbert-style calculus for propositional logic (with appropriate axioms). This is because:
choices: all other rules are derivable from MP and the axioms
explanation: Hilbert calculi are axiom-heavy and rule-light: MP plus a small set of axiom schemas (e.g., K, S, DN) suffice. All natural deduction rules are admissible.
